teams.heading: Andrew Durutalo named Fiji Rugby's new Head of Men's High Performance
teams.body: The Fiji Rugby Union has hired former US international Andrew Durutalo to run its development pathways. Durutalo, who previously captained Fiji Under-21s, is tasked with aligning the structures that feed into the national team. He takes charge as the Flying Fijians prepare for this weekend's Pacific Nations Cup final against Japan. Durutalo stated: 'We need to make sure that our pathway is strengthened and obviously continues to evolve as time goes on.'

lead.why: Andrew Durutalo has been appointed as Fiji Rugby's new Head of Men's High Performance.

teams.heading: Stuart Barnes condemns RFU decision to extend Steve Borthwick England contract
teams.body: Former England fly-half Stuart Barnes has launched a blistering attack on the RFU, accusing them of an "ostrich policy" after they extended head coach Steve Borthwick’s contract to 2028. Barnes argued that Borthwick should have been sacked rather than backed following a run he assessed as failure. Pointing to an embarrassing loss to Italy and regular defeats against Scotland, the pundit claimed England have devolved into a "second-tier Six Nations side" under Borthwick's tenure.

lead.why: Former England international Stuart Barnes has strongly criticised the RFU's decision to hand Steve Borthwick a contract extension.

teams.heading: France compile a formidable scoring record across their past eleven tests
teams.body: Les Bleus have shown ruthless efficiency in front of the posts, accumulating 426 points over their latest eleven internationals. That prolific run yields an average of 38.7 points scored per match. Defensively, the side conceded 291 points in the same span — an average of 26.5 per game. The highlight of this high-scoring period came in February 2026, when France travelled to thrash Wales 54-12 in the Six Nations.

teams.heading: Ben Donnell targets an Ireland call-up after sealing move to Ulster
teams.body: New Ulster signing Ben Donnell is hoping to force his way into the international arena after arriving in Belfast, aiming to catch the eye of Ireland head coach Andy Farrell. The 26-year-old is eligible for Ireland through his Belfast-born father. Having previously represented England at under-18 and under-20 level, Donnell enjoyed spells with London Irish, Gloucester and Cardiff. Now playing in the United Rugby Championship, he hopes to impress Farrell and realise his ambition of playing Test rugby.

teams.heading: Scotland women look to improve after 26-64 defeat to Canada

The team now turns its attention to upcoming matches against New Zealand and Australia. teams.heading: Megan Davey eyes Wales debut after reigniting career at age 26
teams.body: After considering a move into full-time teaching when overlooked for the 2026 Six Nations, Loughborough Lightning’s Megan Davey is now targeting her first international cap. The 26-year-old half-back, who qualifies for Wales through her Llanelli-born grandfather, was called up to the 39-strong squad last month. Davey, who faces internal competition from Keira Bevan and Seren Lockwood, says she is raring to go ahead of the WXV campaign, which begins this Friday against South Africa at Cardiff Arms Park.

teams.heading: Jordan Petaia returns to Australia squad for upcoming Springboks Test match
teams.body: Jordan Petaia has been recalled to the Wallabies squad for the upcoming one-off Test against South Africa in Perth. The utility back returns to the international fold for the first time since the 2023 Rugby World Cup following stints in the NFL and France. Head coach Les Kiss has also drafted in uncapped fly-half Harry McLaughlin-Phillips to replace the injured Carter Gordon, while prop Zane Nonggorr returns to the forward pack. Kiss noted, “We know we still have a lot to work on.”

lead.why: The return of Jordan Petaia to the international fold is the most significant squad development being covered by multiple outlets.

teams.heading: Japan Rugby League One resolves dispute regarding naturalised player status
teams.body: The eligibility dispute surrounding foreign-born players in Japan Rugby League One has been resolved following a formal court settlement. Officials confirmed that players who acquired Japanese nationality before the end of May 2025 will now be treated on a par with native-born players. This decision effectively ends the challenge brought by 24 players, including Timothy Lafaele, who had contested proposed rules that would have restricted the status of naturalised athletes who were not educated in Japan during childhood.

lead.why: The eligibility dispute involving foreign-born, naturalised players has been officially resolved through a court settlement.

teams.heading: Neil Barnes claims officiating hindered All Blacks in series finale
teams.body: Senior assistant coach Neil Barnes has hit out at the officiating during the final Test of the Greatest Rivalry series, suggesting the Springboks benefited from favourable calls. Barnes expressed his frustration with referee Karl Dickson, stating, “Every time they keep getting penalties for bugger all and get to slow the game down, it brings them back into it.” Despite the 43-28 defeat, Barnes insists that the All Blacks are “seriously close” to matching the world champions despite the series loss.

lead.why: The coach's frustration regarding officiating was the most significant point of contention following the series conclusion.

teams.heading: Victor Matfield expects a braver Springboks side as pressure eases
teams.body: Following the conclusion of the four-Test series against New Zealand, Springboks legend Victor Matfield anticipates a shift in strategy. Having secured a 3-1 series victory, Rassie Erasmus’s squad is now expected to favour a more expansive attacking game. Matfield believes the pressure of the intense rivalry previously forced the team to rely heavily on their traditional physical DNA, but notes that with the series won, the world champions are now likely to be "a bit more brave with ball in hand."

lead.why: It outlines the future strategic direction of the team following their successful series victory.
